newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish GPRD road builder prices IPO at PLN 9.
newsitem.headline: Polish GPRD road builder prices IPO at PLN 9.

text.p: Polish road builder Gdanskie Przedsiebiorstwo Robot Drogowych SA (GPRD) set the minimum price of its initial public offering starting this week at nine zlotys per share, the firm's president said.
"The minimum issue price has been set at nine zlotys," Zbigniew Wojciechowski told a meeting with investors on Monday.

Wojciechowski said that GPRD, which plans to enter the main market of the Warsaw bourse, would spend five million zlotys from the issue on road-building equipment and four million zlotys on transport equipment.
He also said the company would invest part of the obtained funds on the capital market, but gave no further details.
Investors will be able to register for up to 550,000 of the firm's shares in the offering of 2,248,700 shares scheduled from November 21 to December 5.
GPRD has already signed an agreement with Wood & Company to guarantee the issue at a stand-by fee of 3.5 percent.

Wojciechowski said the firm expected to make a net profit of more than seven million zlotys this year on sales of 120 million zlotys against 4.6 million zlotys last year on sales of 83 million zlotys.
He said management would propose a dividend for 1996 not greater than 10 to 15 percent of net profit and planned no new share issue for 1997 or 1998.
GPRD is part of the Gdansk Transport Company SA, a consortium including Bechtel international that is bidding to take part in Poland's highway-building programme.
